title: Scaled Rademacher entry lies in $L^2$
statement: Fix $k > 0$ and a vector $x \in \bbr^d$, and let $\mu$ be the joint Rademacher product measure on the sample space of $k \times d$ arrays $\omega = (\omega_{ij})$. Then for every pair of indices $i$ and $j$, the coordinate function $\omega \mapsto \dfrac{x_j}{\sqrt{k}}\,\omega_{ij}$ is square-integrable with respect to $\mu$; that is, it belongs to $L^2(\mu)$.
hypotheses_covered: x is a vector in ℝ^d
i is an index in Fin k
j is an index in Fin d
measure is the joint Rademacher product measure
replaced:
For $k > 0$, $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$, and indices $i,j$, the function
$\omega \mapsto (x_j/\sqrt{k})\,\omega_{ij}$ belongs to $L^2(\mathrm{radJointMeasure})$.
